title: Methamphetamine use, methamphetamine use disorder, and associated overdose deaths among US adults

claims.statement: Among US adults aged 18–64, estimated past-year methamphetamine use rose from about 1.61 million in 2015 to 1.97 million in 2019 (about +22%) and past-year methamphetamine use disorder (DSM-IV criteria) from about 741,000 to 1.09 million (about +47%), while overdose deaths involving psychostimulants other than cocaine rose from 5,526 to 15,489 (+180%), more than half of the 2019 deaths also involving opioids. The paper's headline increases for use (43%) and for use disorder without injection (105%) are calculated from 2016, the lowest year, not from 2015.
claims.magnitude: Use 1,612k (95% CI 1,394–1,829) → 1,971k (1,660–2,282), P for trend 0.002; use disorder 741k (578–905) → 1,091k (816–1,365), P for trend 0.003; deaths 5,526 → 15,489, of which 8,438 also involved opioids in 2019.
